feedback.problem:
What is the radius of convergence $R$ of the series

$$
{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{x}^{n}=1+x+{x}^{2}+{x}^{3}+⋯\,?
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
To apply the ratio test, we define ${a}_{n}={x}^{n}.$ Then, we calculate the ratio of two successive terms and take the limit as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{x}^{n+1}}{{x}^{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|x| \\  & =|x|\end{aligned}
$$

The series converges if $L<1.$ In this case, the convergence condition is satisfied if $|x|<1.$ Therefore, we conclude that the radius of convergence is $R=1.$
